newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-REDS GET SIERRA FROM TIGERS FOR TWO MINOR LEAGUERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-REDS GET SIERRA FROM TIGERS FOR TWO MINOR LEAGUERS.

text.p: The Detroit Tigers on Monday unloaded outfielder Ruben Sierra, but not most of his big salary, to the Cincinnati Reds in exchange for a pair of minor leaguers.

Sierra, who in past deals has been traded for such big name sluggers as Cecil Fielder, Jose Canseco and Danny Tartabull, goes to Cincinnati for minor leaguer outfielder Decomba Conner and pitcher Ben Bailey.
As a condition of the deal, the Tigers agreed to pay $4.875 million of Sierra's $5.5 million 1997 salary, leaving the Reds responsible for about $625,000.
The 31-year-old Sierra was traded by the New York Yankees in July for 1990s home run king Cecil Fielder. The Tigers were looking to avoid Fielder's $9.2 million salary in 1997.
The Reds were seeking a cleanup hitter in the four-time All-Star.

Reds general manager Jim Bowden said the club was in the market for: "a player who had a history of playing every day, the capability to hit 20-25 homers while driving in 80-100 runs, and a player that fit our salary range for that position."
Sierra will be joining his first National League club after spending all 11 of his major league seasons in the American League.
The switch-hitter has a lifetime .270 batting average with 232 home runs and 1,024 RBI. He has averaged 21 homers and 93 RBI per season in his major league career.
Sierra led the league in RBI with 119 in 1989, and batted a career-high .307 in 1991.
